transcript.content: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

I’m here because… my mind keeps sort of going blank. At work, I’ll be looking at the road-closure forms or holding the stop-slow paddle, and suddenly I can’t remember steps I’ve done for years. It’s been… hard to trust myself.
When your mind goes blank, does the world around you ever feel unreal or dreamlike?
I don’t know… I wouldn’t say dreamlike, exactly. It’s more like I just lose the thread for a bit. I haven’t really noticed the world feeling unreal.
During these blank moments, do you ever forget important personal information about yourself?
No… I don’t think so. I know who I am. It’s more just… I lose track of what I’m doing.
Have you been feeling down or depressed lately?
Yeah… I have. Most mornings I wake up with this… heavy sadness, I guess. Like the day’s already gone bad before I even get up.
Have you lost interest in things you usually enjoy?

Yeah… I guess so. I used to be the one setting things up—choir rides, garden swaps, snacks for the kids’ basketball stuff. Now I’ll just sit there staring at my phone for hours and… I don’t even answer people. I just can’t make myself care enough to.
Have you been moving or speaking noticeably more slowly than usual?

Yeah… I think so. It takes me forever just to bathe and get dressed, get to the door. My family says I move like I’m underwater.

But then other times I can’t sit still… I pace in the hallway and wring my hands. I don’t know. It’s embarrassing.
Have these memory problems led you to make mistakes at work?

Yeah… it has. I started messing up the road-closure paperwork, or just not finishing it. And with traffic safety stuff, I’d second-guess myself so much I didn’t feel like I could trust what I was doing.

I stopped being reliable, I guess. People noticed. My family did too… I’d pulled back from choir and volunteering and them, and they finally kind of… brought me in.
Do you find yourself worrying a lot, even when there isn’t an immediate problem to solve?
I don’t know… I worry some, I guess. But I’m not sure it’s like that. I haven’t really been keeping track of it.
Did these mind-blanking and memory problems start around the same time as the sadness and loss of interest?

Yeah… around the same stretch of time, I think. For months now, when I’ve been waking up sad and guilty and not really eating… that’s also when the voices and the messages from trucks or radios have been happening.

I don’t like talking about it, but… yes, it all kind of overlaps.
When you hear the voices or messages, do they tell you that you’re guilty or deserve to be punished?

Yeah… sometimes it feels like that. Like they’re pointing at everything I didn’t do right.

I keep going over things with my friend, and choir, and my family… all the ways I failed them. And then it feels like I’m just… useless. Like maybe I deserve whatever’s coming.
Do the voices or messages ever happen when you are not feeling depressed?

Yeah… I think so. Before it got really bad, I was still going to work and church and everything, but I’d already started hearing my name sometimes.

And… I thought signs, or the radio, were kind of… sending things about me. That went on for a few weeks, I guess.
Were the voices or messages happening for at least 2 weeks during a time when you were not feeling depressed?

I think… yes. It was a few weeks, before things got so low. I was still making it to work and church, but I was already hearing my name and feeling like signs or the radio were sending messages about me.
Have people told you that your speech has been hard to follow or that you jump from one idea to another?
I don’t know… maybe sometimes. People have told me I’m not making much sense, but I don’t always notice it when I’m talking.
Even when you are not feeling depressed, do you still find yourself emotionally flat or not caring about being around other people?

Yeah… I guess so. I used to be the one setting things up—choir rides, garden swaps, snacks for the kids’ basketball and all that. Now I can just sit there for hours looking at my phone and… not even feel like answering people.
Were there times when you heard voices or believed the radio or signs were sending messages about you, but you were not feeling depressed?

Yes… there were a few weeks like that. I wasn’t really down yet, not the way it got later. I was still going to work and church, but I was already hearing my name sometimes, and… thinking the radio or signs were meant for me.
For about a month or longer, were you hearing voices or thinking the radio or signs were sending messages about you?
Yes… longer than a month. It’s been… about a year and four months, with the voices and feeling like signs or trucks or the radio were meant for me.
For at least one month, were the voices or messages happening often enough that they were a major problem for you?
Yes… it was often enough. The voices, and feeling like signs or trucks or the radio were messages for me… that’s been going on about a year and four months.
Have these problems overall been going on continuously for at least 6 months?
Yes… it’s been more than six months. About a year and eight months, I think. It started after my closest friend died.
During the times when you were hearing voices or felt signs or the radio were sending messages, were you ever completely free of depression?

Yes… I think there were a few weeks like that. Before the depression got really bad, I was still going to work and church, but I was already hearing my name and thinking signs and the radio were… meant for me.
Looking over the whole time since these problems began, have you been depressed for most of that time?
Yes… most of the time, I think. It’s like that heaviness was there for most of it, even when the other things got a little quieter.

target_item.name: Additional Requirement 3
target_item.manifestation: Before the depression got so deep, there were several weeks when I was still getting to work and church but already hearing my name and believing signs and radios were sending messages about me.
target_item.reason: The doctor is asking whether there were periods of psychotic symptoms, like voices or messages, when depression was absent.

patient.answer: Yes… I think there were a few weeks like that. Before the depression got really bad, I was still going to work and church, but I was already hearing my name and thinking signs and the radio were… meant for me.

doctor.intent: Determine whether prominent mood episodes have been present for most of the total duration of the psychotic illness, which best distinguishes schizoaffective disorder from schizophrenia.
doctor.question: Looking over the whole time since these problems began, have you been depressed for most of that time?

target_item.name: Additional Requirement 2
target_item.manifestation: Looking back, most of this whole illness has been spent under that heavy depression, even during times when the voices or suspicious thoughts were quieter.
target_item.reason: The doctor is asking whether depression has been present for most of the overall illness duration, which directly matches Criterion C.

patient.answer: Yes… most of the time, I think. It’s like that heaviness was there for most of it, even when the other things got a little quieter.

inference.note: Psychotic symptoms were present for at least 2 weeks in the absence of depression, excluding mood disorder with psychotic symptoms; depressive episodes have been present for most of the total illness duration, favoring schizoaffective disorder, depressive type, over schizophrenia.

opening_question.intent: Understand the patient's main reason for seeking help today
opening_question.question: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient has persistent psychotic symptoms (auditory hallucinations, ideas/delusions of reference, possible disorganized speech, negative symptoms) lasting well over 1 month and continuously over 6 months, together with a major depressive syndrome characterized by depressed mood, anhedonia, psychomotor change, guilt, poor appetite, and functional decline. Crucially, psychotic symptoms were present for at least 2 weeks in the absence of a depressive episode, while depressive symptoms were present for most of the illness duration. This pattern is most consistent with schizoaffective disorder, depressive type.
